calibration.calibration_regime_meaning: B (direct effects only): damage curves are read as each agent's direct dependency, interaction edges add the indirect part

parameters.name: model.trophic_transfer_efficiency
parameters.note: Midpoint of the 5-20% energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels (the textbook range following Lindeman 1942; from memory, verify). The midpoint is a choice, not a measurement.

parameters.name: model.trophic_amplification_exponent
parameters.note: No source: damps the pyramid ratio to 1.6-4.1× amplification for trophic levels 1-3.

parameters.name: carbon_price.year0
parameters.note: Social cost of carbon. The 2020-emissions value is used as the year-0 price: EPA's own path gives about $215 for 2026 emissions, so year-0 carbon damage is understated by about 13%. 2020 euros, no inflation adjustment.
parameters.source: US EPA (2023), Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Table ES.1: $190/tCO2 (2020 emissions, 2020 USD, 2% near-term rate), at the ECB 2020 average rate of 1.1422 USD/EUR

parameters.name: carbon_price.growth
parameters.note: 60-year average of a decelerating path (1.6%/yr in 2020-2050, 1.2%/yr in 2030-2080).

parameters.name: resource.area_ha
parameters.note: Units / reference density of 250 trees/ha. Chosen so the per-tree carbon gives ~200 t CO2/ha.

parameters.name: resource.unit_value
parameters.note: Revenue per tree felled (one-off); no market source.

parameters.name: resource.safe_threshold_ratio
parameters.note: Safe extraction threshold; under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.

parameters.name: agents.annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. Step 8g.6 (the owner's answer: convert international dollars to euros everywhere): 2,861 x 0.808165 = EUR 2,312.16/ha/yr in 2007 euros at Spanish purchasing power (it was used at face value as EUR 2,848, from figures partly typed from memory: 3,000 - 152; now read in Table 2). Not inflated to a later price year and no income adjustment (the owner's decision for benefit transfers, Step 8d.5). Climate regulation is left out because carbon is valued only by gaia.carbon (decision D3). A global temperate-forest mean, not a site valuation. Converted from Int$ (2007 prices: value Int$2,861) at 0.808165 € per Int$, the PPP factor for household consumption, Spain 2007 (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, World Bank); no income or price-year adjustment.
parameters.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (read in full): temperate forest, total economic value Int$3,013/ha/yr minus climate regulation Int$152 = Int$2,861/ha/yr (2007 international dollars, 2007 price level; 58 estimates, Table 3); converted to EUR with the World Bank's PPP conversion factor for household final consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, the 'private consumption' series de Groot et al. used), Spain, 2007: 0.808165 EUR per international $ (World Development Indicators, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?date=2007&format=json, read 13 October 2026; gaia/currency.py)

parameters.name: damage.threshold_logistic_steepness
parameters.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B).

parameters.note: 2% relative price change of ecosystem services. Above the estimates of Drupp et al. (2024), 1.28%/yr for forests (CI 0.85-1.70) and 1.66%/yr aggregate (CI 1.40-1.92); kept until Step 8. Below the discount rate, so the PV converges.
